name: Reed Green
lede: Reed Green is a muted olive, named for the marsh plant, recorded by Ridgway in 1912 and matched today by the paint standard RAL 6013.

sections.title: A reed-colored olive
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature places this hue at plate XVII, hue 25', tone k, and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary gives a first recorded date of 1892, at plate 19 D 2 [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files it as block 119, a light yellow green, and the German paint standard RAL lists a close approximation as RAL 6013 [1]. ColorHub's data ties the name to reed, the marsh plant, though the books consulted do not spell out the connection in full [2].

The nearest named color is [[kronberg-s-green|Kronberg's Green]], 2.7 units away and a touch yellower; [[yellowish-olive|Yellowish Olive]] sits 4.7 units off [2]. [[pois-green|Pois Green]], another muted green in this same wave of names, is 5.7 units away [2]. In LCH terms Reed Green measures lightness 51, chroma 20, hue 111 degrees [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds Reed Green in 1,104 of 23,781 paintings, 4.64 percent, as photographed, more common than 85 percent of the archive's named colors [3]. Peter Snayers is its most devoted painter, present in 5 of his 16 works here at 6.2 times his baseline, and it peaks in the 1900s, in 74 of 1,674 paintings, at 1.8 times the expected rate [3]. It most often turns up as a hidden color, tucked into shadow, in 38 percent of its paintings [3]. The earliest match is dated 916, nine hundred ninety-six years before Ridgway's 1912 record of the name — a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof of the pigment itself, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].
